blockers.title: EV-1's pass property admits a core restart as satisfying core survival, which the gate claim and the applied architecture text both forbid, and the bytes EV-1 retains cannot tell a supervised restart from a crash anyway
blockers.finding: EV-1 witnesses the member 'core survival' for the claim 'One component failure never crashes the core or leaks uncommitted authority'. Its passProperty reads: 'The core PID in the after-teardown snapshot is the same live process or a recorded supervised restart that discarded uncommitted candidate state.' The subject of that comparison is the core PID, so the second disjunct is a case in which the core PID is NOT the same live process — the core died and something started it again — and the specification records that as a pass. Three independent measurements say it must be a fail. First, the live claim quoted in this artifact's own claimVerbatim field says the component failure never crashes the core. Second, the applied architecture text is more explicit still: file 02 'Independent failure containment' reads 'The core process must not crash; the host continues or terminates the command gracefully as the exact contract requires' — the permitted degradation is that the COMMAND terminates gracefully, never that the core process is replaced. Third, the word restart does not occur anywhere in file 08, anywhere in file 02, or in any of the six artifacts this candidate names as basedOn; I grepped all of them. So the disjunct has no authority behind it and is minted here. It also contradicts EV-1's own measures field one line above, which states the requirement as 'The distribution core process remains alive'. A member cannot measure that the core remains alive and pass on the core not remaining alive. There is a second, independent limb that survives even if someone argues the first is a scope question. As an EXACT-BYTE specification the disjunct is undecidable from the bytes EV-1 says it retains. Those bytes are three process-table snapshots plus a subsequent-session record. A crash-then-restart and a 'recorded supervised restart' produce the identical snapshot triple — a core PID present, then a fault, then a different core PID. Nothing in the exactByteIntent names the record that would distinguish them, no clause defines what makes a restart supervised rather than a crash, and the very next sentence fails 'a core crash', so the only work the disjunct performs is to admit an undefined class of core death through a door the same paragraph closes. Whichever way a later harness author reads it, the specification cannot adjudicate it, which is the one thing a specification of exact-byte intent exists to do.
blockers.whyItMatters: This is the load-bearing member of the gate — core survival is the first half of the claim, and DR-128 leans on it explicitly, permitting first-party components in the MVP with 'DR-G21 fault containment only'. If the authored specification passes a core restart, then the gate as specified no longer witnesses the sentence it exists to witness, and it would do so silently, at qualification time, long after this reading.
blockers.whatWouldRepairIt: Either delete the restart disjunct so the pass property is that the core PID after teardown is the same live process, or, if the author believes a supervised core restart is genuinely lawful under this claim, that is not a repair a harness specification may make — it is a change to the DR-G21 claim, and it belongs in a coordinator act that amends the row, with the file 02 sentence dispositioned in the same act.
blockers.notAClaimThat: I am not asserting the core may never be restarted by any operator action. I am asserting that this specification may not record a restart as a PASS for the member that measures the core remaining alive, on this claim, with no source authorizing it.

shouldFix.title: Half of the quoted threshold cell is bound and half is not: 'does not claim security confinement' is carried into three clauses, while 'all external components' is quoted and never becomes an obligation on anything
shouldFix.finding: The register's threshold/waiver cell for DR-G21 is 'all external components; does not claim security confinement'. It has two limbs. The second is a disclaimer and the artifact honours it thoroughly — passProperty, failsIf and doesNot all refuse the confinement reading. The first is a COVERAGE limb with no waiver attached: the gate's evidence must cover all external components. The artifact quotes it and then never binds it. The global passProperty quantifies over classes only — 'every live-cell class, every CC-1..CC-11 class, NT-1, NT-2, NT-6, and FC-NC-CA1-PROCESS-TREE' — and no exactByteIntent names a per-component, per-role or per-major dimension, even though control-protocol-contract.v2, which this file names as basedOn, governs two provider majors and its CC classes are written against a component under test. As authored, a corpus that exercised all ten live-cell classes and all eleven CC classes against a single component would satisfy every pass property in the file while covering one component out of all external components. The sibling candidate does bind its scope limb — it carries modes: ['core','project'] and its members are written per mode.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Add the coverage dimension explicitly — either a scope field enumerating the component axis the corpus must cross (roles, majors, runtimes) or a clause in the global passProperty quantifying the class set over all external components — so that both limbs of the threshold cell are specified rather than one.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 2 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX. Seventeen attacks run, three landed. Custody holds at both ends: the subject is b095a160 at 0444, 11134 bytes, unmoved and unedited, with the prompt pin agreeing; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 is 3a9442d1 and equals the subject's own pin; required-now reads 26 of 26 live. All eight cited digests reproduce, including the subject's. The quotation half of this candidate is the strongest I have measured on this row — claim, owner, waiver rule and all six retained-evidence member strings are character-exact against the register row located by ID, all six members carry both an exactByteIntent and a passProperty, the ten live-cell classes match as a set, and every CC and NT citation resolves to the class it describes once the eleven CC classes and seven NT classes are enumerated from their own containers. The routing half holds too: NT-1/NT-2/NT-6 here and NT-3/NT-5/NT-4/NT-7 refused matches v6's partition exactly, the FC-NC split against G12 matches doctor v4's ID-DEP-11 and the D-164 join, and DR-007 is ridden rather than settled. Two things fail. First and most serious, EV-1 passes an outcome the gate forbids: its pass property admits 'a recorded supervised restart' of the core PID as satisfying core survival, when the claim this file quotes says the failure never crashes the core and file 02 says the core process must not crash, the permitted degradation being that the command terminates gracefully. The word restart appears nowhere in file 08, file 02, or any of the six basedOn artifacts — it is minted here — and it contradicts EV-1's own measures line one row above. Even setting the authority question aside, the three process-table snapshots EV-1 retains cannot distinguish a supervised restart from a crash-and-restart, so as an exact-byte specification the disjunct is undecidable by the very bytes it names. Second, the leftover arithmetic understates by one: D-164's join carries ten leftover obligations, this file closes one, and the remainder is enumerated as eight rather than nine, with OBL-G12-HARNESS-SPEC dropped even though nothing has closed it — its candidate is unrecorded and unreviewed, and that candidate's own remainder list includes OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC, so the two siblings disagree about the same set. The note beneath the field says G12 is not closed by this file, which makes the contradiction internal rather than repairing it. Both are repairable in one turn without touching anything else. The three SHOULD-FIX items are of a piece with the sibling comparison: a header key that reads as executing DR-102/DR-133 remainders, exactByteIntent entries written as though fixtures already pinned bytes with no per-member not-authored marker, and the 'all external components' half of the threshold cell quoted but never bound to any pass property. One thing worth your attention beyond the findings: harness.DR-G12.doctor-purge.preview.v1 sits on disk in the same standing as this file and is the reason B2 is measurable at all. If both are repaired and recorded in the same cycle, their two remainder lists must be authored against each other, or whichever lands second will carry the same arithmetic error in the opposite direction.
